editorial.headline: Energy Storage, With Bali’s Risk Line in View
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and Bali does not block its PMA registration under the stated moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the storage infrastructure behind petroleum and natural gas: receiving, collecting, holding and releasing petroleum, petroleum fuels, gas fuels and/or processed products. The storage location may be above ground, below ground or on the water’s surface. The scope is specific about those storage functions, and extends to operations in free-trade zones, physical commodity storage sites, storage run through a warehouse-receipt system, and cold warehouses used for oil and natural-gas storage.

The brief also reaches beyond conventional hydrocarbons. It includes carbon-free fuels used as energy carriers—hydrogen, ammonia and other compounds—stored in geological formations, through gas compression, in solid or liquid form, or in other forms. In other words, the classification follows the practical cycle of receipt, accumulation, containment and release across a broad range of energy-storage formats. It is open to businesses operating at small, medium or large scale, without changing that central storage focus.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today: the record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk. For this activity, however, the record states that the OSS risk at large scale is Medium-High/High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium.

That distinction is the essential one. The national position permits full foreign ownership, while the Bali position does not introduce a separate foreign-ownership figure or partnership condition in the record. Its status is recorded as “OK_or_HIGHER_RISK,” reflecting the stated large-scale risk position. For an operator considering this classification, the question is whether the real operation performs the storage activity described here, and at which scale—not whether Bali applies a blanket PMA prohibition to it.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today because it is not blocked by the stated moratorium.
